# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-core-low-threading

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests **Message Board / Threading** in isolation on the 10-pair `core` subset with `vertex_ai/gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter). Outgoing messages receive monotonic run-scoped IDs (`m1`, `m2`, ...) with `--reply-to <id>` and `--resolve` flags, an active open-thread footer on every turn, and a harness-pinned active thread board preserved across 28K context compactions. Compared against `coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-core-low-stepcounter` (4/10).

## Observations

- Passed dropped from 4/10 to 1/10 (`dottxt_ai_outlines_task/1655`), mirroring the `flash_10` drop (from 6/10 to 2/10) on `gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking), even though merge conflicts decreased from 6 to 4 (`go_chi_task/27`, `pallets_click_task/2800`, `pallets_jinja_task/1559`, and `pallets_jinja_task/1621` all merged cleanly).
- Protocol mechanics functioned cleanly (30 threads opened, 26 resolved = 87% resolution rate across 142 messages, with only 2 syntax-validation rejections), but 280 per-turn `[Open threads (...)]` reminders diverted `gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking) toward thread-closing chatter instead of finishing independent feature verification (`llama_index_task/17244`, `pallets_click_task/2800`, and `pallets_jinja_task/1559` each passed Feature A while Feature B submitted an incomplete patch).
